lines.text: Hi, I'm Sindy! Today, sind meets your AI assistant.
Wish your AI assistant could create and check Slurm clusters for you, not just write code? With the MCP server built into sind, it can.
Setup takes one command: sind mcp claude enable registers sind with Claude Desktop.
For VS Code or Cursor, use their names instead, and disable takes it back.
Or register it by hand, with this entry in the MCP config of your editor. It runs sind mcp start.
Almost every sind command becomes a tool, except the interactive ones and those that print secrets.
Tools are named after their commands, like sind create cluster, and sind mcp tools exports the full list.
Each tool also carries a hint. Get tools are marked read-only, while exec, the create and delete tools and most power tools are marked destructive.
So your client can pause for your approval first.
One server for several clients? sind mcp stream serves it over HTTP, on port eighty eighty.
Every request needs a bearer token. The stream shows the file that holds it, but never the token itself, then a client config you can paste.
A word of caution: this server is no sandbox. Every tool runs sind with your own Docker access.
Approve a create call only after reading its flags, and set data to volume, so your host files stay out.
Give an agent these tools only where you'd trust it to run sind as you.
So: one command hooks sind into your editor, every tool carries a hint for your client, and you read create calls before approving them.
Next up, the guide for CI pipelines. See you there!
